title: Regional Fallback Zero-Trust Routing Playbook
author: Priya Singh
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook documents the decision flow, operator procedures, configuration artifacts, and dashboard checks for performing region-level fallback routing under a zero-trust posture. It is intended for platform operators and SREs who must preserve application SLAs while maintaining cryptographic and policy boundaries during regional failover.

Scope: Applies to L7 request routing for inference endpoints, internal control-plane traffic (controlplane.redwood-inference), and telemetry egress. Does NOT modify tenant data at rest or change model weights.

Goals and constraints
- Preserve p99 latency SLOs for interactive tenants where possible. Target: p99 < 450ms after failover for priority-tenants.
- Maintain zero-trust authentication for cross-region routing (mTLS + OIDC token exchange).
- Avoid mass-credential exfiltration: do not embed long-lived credentials in routing configuration.
- Prefer model-variant fallback (smaller/quantized variant) before re-routing traffic across jurisdictions.

Owner and escalation
- Primary oncall: Platform Operators (platform-oncall rotation).
- Secondary: Runtime Reliability (runtime-rel team).
- Pager escalation: use the oncall rota in PagerDuty, tag incidents with component:regional-routing.

Preconditions (automated checks to run before executing manual steps)
1) Confirm region health summary dashboard: all dataplane pods reporting Ready > 95% and GPU utilization < 92%. Query: sum(kube_pod_status_ready{region=~"us-.*"}) / count(kube_pod_status_ready{region=~"us-.*"})
2) Verify SLO burn: tokenized_sli_burn{route=~"/v1/generate|/v1/chat"} < 0.25 in last 5m.
3) Ensure KMS cross-region key policy allows transient-wrap for fallback exchange.
4) Validate OPA policy test-suite passes locally (opa test ./policies)

Decision matrix (high-level)
- Severity: Control plane outage (no) | Dataplane partial outage (yes) | Dataplane full outage (yes)
- If partial outage and prioritization score > 0.7 => route priority-tenants only to adjacent region with model-variant fallback enabled.
- If full outage in region and adjacent region capacity < 25% spare => enable degraded-mode local queue + burst-credit gate.

Runbook: step-by-step procedure
1) Initial triage (0-5m)
   a) Open incident channel and paste region health snapshot.
   b) Run 'region-health-check --region=eu-west-1 --include=dataplane,controlplane' (internal CLI).
   c) If controlplane healthy and dataplane degraded, proceed to step 2.
2) Preflight policy & auth checks (5-10m)
   a) Confirm cross-region mTLS trust chain: `openssl s_client -connect gateway-eu-west-1:8443 -servername controlplane` (expect cert CN includes region-allow-list).
   b) Run OIDC token exchange smoke using ephemeral service account: `rcli oidc:exchange --aud=regional-fallback --expiry=5m` (expect token returned).
   c) Verify KMS wrapping permitted for target region: `kms-validate-wrap --key=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:...`
3) Canary routing (10-25m)
   a) Create a canary route that matches 2% traffic from the failing region for high-priority tenants. Example Routing YAML (apply via platform-router):

```
apiVersion: routing.platform.redwood/v1
kind: Route
metadata:
  name: regional-fallback-canary-eu-to-us
spec:
  match: 
    - prefix: "/v1/generate"
      tenant_priority: "priority"
  filters:
    - name: auth-mtls-bridge
  destination:
    host: router-us-east-1.internal
    weight: 2
    headers:
      x-fallback: "eu->us-canary"
```

   b) Observe metrics for 5 full p99 windows (typical 5m each). Key queries listed in Observability section.
4) Incremental ramp (25-60m)
   a) If canary p99 < target and error-rate delta < 0.5%, increase weight in controlled steps: 2% -> 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%. Each step: wait for 2 p99 aggregation windows, validate tracing spans for auth latency below 60ms.
   b) If auth failures occur (5xx auth errors), rollback to previous weight and open follow-up task to fix policy.
5) Full cutover (60-90m)
   a) After 100% validation, convert temporary route to permanent fallback with explicit auditing metadata and automated TTL for reversal.
   b) Create incident annotation linking to route change and KMS wrap operation id.
6) Post-cutover cleanup (90-180m)
   a) Validate billing/telemetry tags for cross-region egress.
   b) Run regression tests on a representative prompt set (see 'Validation suites' below).

Rollback criteria and emergency rollback steps
- Rollback immediately if: error rate increases > 1% absolute, p99 > 2x target, auth errors > 0.2% of requests, or downstream model responses indicate corruption (LLM quality regression alert).
- Emergency rollback CLI: `platform-router rollback --route=regional-fallback-canary-eu-to-us --to-weight=0` and `platform-router remove --route=regional-fallback-canary-eu-to-us --grace=5m`
- If rollback fails: disable routing rules and enable local degraded queue: `platform-queue enable-degraded --region=eu-west-1 --duration=2h` and page runtime-reliability.

Observability and dashboards
- Add/verify the following panels on regional-fallback dashboard:
  - Per-region p50/p95/p99 latency for /v1/generate and /v1/chat (group by tenant_priority).
  - Auth handshake latency (mTLS) and OIDC token exchange success rate.
  - Cross-region egress bytes and billing tags.
  - Route weight vs error-rate heatmap (1m resolution).

Suggested metric expressions (PromQL examples):
- p99 latency: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=~"/v1/.*",region="eu-west-1"}[5m])) by (le))`
- mTLS handshake failures: `sum(rate(tls_handshake_errors_total{peer_region!=""}[1m]))`
- OIDC failures: `sum(rate(oidc_exchange_error_total[5m])) by (error_type)`

Configuration artifacts and policy examples
- OPA policy snippet (guarding cross-region):
```
package routing.zero_trust

allow {
  input.destination_region == "us-east-1"
  input.tenant_priority == "priority"
  valid_token(input.oidc)
}

valid_token(t) {
  t.iss == "https://auth.redwood-inference"
  t.exp > time.now_ns() / 1000000000
}
```

- Route manifest fields (table):
| Field | Description | Example |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| match.prefix | Request path prefix | /v1/generate |
| match.tenant_priority | Priority bucket label | priority |
| destination.host | Upstream routing host | router-us-east-1.internal |
| destination.weight | Traffic percent weight (0-100) | 2 |
| filters | Chain of policy bridges (auth, audit) | [auth-mtls-bridge, audit-proxy] |
| metadata.audit_tag | Freeform audit tag for change logs | eu->us-jan-18-cutover |

Access control and auditing
- All route changes must be applied via the platform-router CLI or the UI with RBAC role: routing.operator. Manual etcd edits are forbidden.
- Each routing change must include `metadata.audit_tag` and reference the incident id. Automated commit hooks validate presence.
- Audit logs for cross-region KMS wrap operations must be captured and stored in the secure audit bucket with 365-day retention.

Validation suites (post-cutover)
- Latency smoke: synthetic runner (srunner) executes 2000 representative prompts (mix of short/long) and produces metrics. Pass threshold: p99 < target and error-rate < 0.5%.
- Quality smoke: run eval subset (eval-suite/regional-fallback/quality-100) and compare BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity delta < 1.5% vs baseline.
- Security smoke: run penetration-tokenization test to verify no header leakage across tenant boundaries.

Runbook example checklist (single-page)
1) [ ] Incident channel created and health snapshot posted
2) [ ] OIDC + mTLS verification passed
3) [ ] Canary route applied (2%)
4) [ ] Canary p99 & error rates within thresholds
5) [ ] Incremental ramp steps completed with checks
6) [ ] Final route hardened with audit metadata
7) [ ] Post-cutover validation suites passed

Known limitations and follow-ups
- Cross-region egress cost spike risk: ensure finance has been notified via the cost-ops flow if predicted egress > $5k/hr.
- Some on-prem private deployments may require manual KMS bridge installation; see eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging for instructions.
- Future work: automate canary ramp using adaptive ramp heuristics tied to SLI burn. See roadmap ticket ROAD-1824.

Appendices
A) Quick reference CLI commands
- region-health-check --region=<r> --include=dataplane,controlplane
- rcli oidc:exchange --aud=regional-fallback --expiry=5m
- platform-router apply --file=canary.yaml --dry-run=false
- platform-router rollback --route=<name> --to-weight=<n>
- platform-queue enable-degraded --region=<r> --duration=2h

B) Rollout example timeline (operator estimate)
- T0 (0m): incident declared
- T+10m: preflight checks complete
- T+25m: canary applied and first evaluation window
- T+90m: full cutover if all validations pass
- T+180m: post-cutover validations complete and incident closed

C) Contacts and ownership
- Platform Operators: platform-oncall@redwood.ai
- Runtime Reliability: runtime-reliability@redwood.ai
- Security (KMS/OIDC): security-crypto@redwood.ai
- Cost ops: cost-ops@redwood.ai
